la:adj:intolerabilis.html:
in-tŏlĕrābĭlis, e, adj.
Act., that cannot bear a thing, impatient (ante-class.): didicisset id ferre, et non esset intolerabilis, Afran. ap. (Com. Fragm. v. 255 Rib.). —
Pass., that cannot be borne, insupportable, intolerable (class.): sumptus,: odor,: frigus,: dolor, : potentia,: vitium,: verba,: insolentia,: saevitia,; : regium nomen Romae,: Cornelius arrogantiā,: vitium,: injuria, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 3, 3, 2.—Comp.: multo intolerabilior,: factum,: intolerabilius nihil est quam femina dives,.—
Irresistible: vis Romanorum,.— Adv.: intŏlĕrābĭlĭter, insupportably, intolerably, .

la:verb:intono.html:
in-tŏno, ŭi (āvi), 1, v. n.,
to thunder (class.).
Lit.: partibus intonuit caeli Pater ipse sinistris, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 47, 106: cum deus intonuit,: intonuere poli,: pater omnipotens ter intonuit,; 9, 361: deus majestatis intonuit, et saep.—Impers.: intonuit laevum,; .—
Transf., to make a noise, resound: et clipeum super intonat ingens,: concussa arma intonuere,: unus praecipue servus tam valde intonuit, ut,: ingenti latratu canis,: Eurus Intonat Aegaeo,.—
Pregn., to bring down with a thundering sound: clavam superne intonat,; cf.: Eois intonata fluctibus hiems,.—
Trop., to cry out vehemently; to thunder forth: hesternā contione intonuit vox perniciosa tribuni,: exsurgit atque intonat ore,: intonet horrendum,: cum haec intonuisset plenus irae,: minas,; : silvae intonuere,; . —Poet.: (Fortuna) simul intonuit, proxima

quaeque fugat, has threatened, : armis urbi,.

la:verb:intorqueo.gloss: to twist, turn or spin around; wrench, sprain; contort
senses: to twist, turn or spin around; wrench, sprain; contort
to brandish, hurl or throw towards
to throw or cast against or upon
la:verb:intorqueo.html:
in-torquĕo, torsi, tortum, 2, v. a.,
to twist, turn round, turn to; to wrench, sprain (class.).
Lit.: mentum in dicendo,to distort,: oculos,: caulem,: talum, to sprain, Auct. B. Hisp. 38: vereor, ne Pompeio quid oneris imponam, μή μοι Γοργείην κεφαλὴν δεινοῖο πελώρου intorqueat, .—Pass. or with se, to twist or wrap itself: involvulus, quae in pampini folio intorta implicat se,: cum subito ... procella nubibus intorsit sese,: ipsi palmites intorquentur,. —
Transf.
To brandish, hurl, or throw towards: hastam tergo,to launch at its back,: jaculum alicui,to hurl against one,; ; : telum,: saxum,: telum in hostem,; . —
To throw into confusion: orationem,; cf. mores,to corrupt, pervert,.—
Trop., to cast upon, throw out against: alternis versibus intorquentur inter fratres gravissimae contumeliae,: vocem diram,.— Hence, intortus, a, um, P. a., twisted, wound; crisped, curled; trailed, prolonged; perplexed, involved; distorted, corrupted: spirae modo,: intorto circa bracchium pallio,wound about my arm,: paludamentum,wrapped round,: angues intorti capillis Eumenidum,entwined,: capilli,curled,; : sonus concisus, intortus,: noctuae intorto carmine occinunt,: rudentes,twisted, made by twisting,: funes,—Adv.: intortē, windingly, crookedly: intortius,.— Transf.: hoc dicere, August. de Nat. et .

la:adj:intonsus.html:
intonsus, a, um, adj.
2. in-tondeo
,
unshorn.
Lit.: scindens dolore identidem intonsam comam, Acc. ap. : capilli,: crinis,: Cynthius,: deus,; (4, 12), 52: comae,; : mentum,: caput,: ora,i. e. not yet shaved,: oves,.—With Gr. acc.: Rhodanique comas intonsa juventus,.—
Transf.: montes, i. e. leafy (covered with grass, herbs, or bushes), : quercus intonsaque caelo Attollunt capita,leafy,: myrtus,.—Of the old Romans, who neither cut their hair nor shaved their beards: tonsores in Italiam venere post Romam conditam anno CCCCLIV., antea intonsi fuere,: : avi,bearded,. —
Trop., unpolished, rude: homines intonsi et inculti,: Getae,.
